subject: POC Observability Plan and Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: POC Observability Plan and Next Steps

Hi Alice — great call today, thanks for walking through your evaluation goals. This thread is a quick post-call recap and proposed observability plan for the POC so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners.

Summary of the call (1:1):
- Goals: validate latency and cost at 95th percentile across expected QPS; ensure accuracy/regression checks on a representative prompt set; confirm logs/traces for incident debug.
- POC scope: 3-week sandbox connecting FintechX staging traffic to Redwood Dedicated instance with a 1M token test workload and live inference sampling.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: p95 latency < 350ms for 512-token workloads under nominal load.
2) Cost: tokens/unit and projected monthly spend within the threshold you shared (<= $X/month — pls confirm).
3) Reliability: no more than 0.5% error rate on requests and graceful fallback when capacity constrained.
4) Observability: dashboards + traces available within first 3 business days; logs exporting to your Splunk/Cloud Logging with retention to match your policy.

Observability plan (what Redwood will deliver):
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboard templates for token-level cost, per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), error rates, cache hit rates, and token throughput.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry-compatible spans for request lifecycle, model selection, and kernel-level fallbacks.
- Logs: structured JSON request/response metadata (no raw PII) with fields: request_id, route, model_version, prompt_hash, latency_ms, token_count, error_code. Exports: S3/Cloud Logging/Splunk connector.
- Metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, token_throughput, cache_hit_rate, model_fallback_rate, per-token-cost_estimate.
- Alerts: we will provide alert runbooks for latency and error surge (>3x baseline) and cost anomalies.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope and NDAs/access.
- Day 1-6: infra hookup, verify sample traffic and dashboards deployed to FintechX Grafana tenant or shared Grafana.
- Week 1-2: run deterministic workload (1M tokens) + sampling traffic.
- Week 3: analysis, regression checks, and final review.

Owners:
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) — commercial and timeline owner.
- Redwood Infra/Integration: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@redwood.ai) — instrumentation, dashboard deployment.
- Redwood Engineering (on-call): Aditya Rao (aditya.rao@redwood.ai) — tracing/log-export and kernel fallback config.
- FintechX POC lead: please confirm (I have Alice and Bob added here).

Immediate asks from FintechX:
- Confirm success criteria and budget threshold for cost target.
- Confirm preferred POC start date (we suggested Apr 6).
- Provide Splunk/Cloud Logging write credentials or an S3 bucket.

Attachments: redwood-poc-observability-checklist.pdf (checklist and sample dashboard link).

If this all looks good I'll kick off the infra invite and schedule a 30-min tech handoff with Marcus and Aditya on Monday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Patel <bob.patel@fintechx.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan and Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: we confirm latency target p95 < 350ms for 512-token workloads. For cost, our internal limit for the POC is $12k/month equivalent; please confirm Redwood's cost estimate for the proposed workload profile.
- Reliability: we'd like the error rate to be <0.2% for production-like traffic; for the POC we can accept up to 0.5% as you listed.
- Observability: Splunk is our preferred destination for logs; I can provision a write key and send it to your infra team. Retention requirement: 90 days.

POC start: Apr 6 works for us. Our POC team will be Alice Chen (me) and Bob Patel (platform eng). We'd like the tech handoff on Apr 6 at 10:00 AM PT.

Questions: 
1) Can you confirm that no customer prompt text will be stored in logs?
2) What sampling rate do you recommend for tracing for the POC (we want high fidelity for error cases but avoid cost blowup)?

Thanks — I'll await the checklist and the Grafana templates.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Director of Engineering, FintechX
alice.chen@fintechx.com

Hi Alice — thanks for the confirmations and the retention note. Quick answers:
- No plaintext customer prompts will be stored in logs. We log a prompt_hash (one-way) and metadata only.
- Tracing sampling recommendation: for the POC we suggest 5-10% head sampling plus 100% sampling for error traces. If you prefer higher fidelity we can increase to 20% for the deterministic 1M token run.

Next steps I'll action today:
1) Share the redwood-poc-observability-checklist.pdf and the Grafana dashboard templates (Drive link below).
2) Marcus will send a short integration checklist for Splunk and a sample ingest role.
3) Schedule tech handoff: Apr 6 10:00 AM PT (I'll send the invite).

Hi all — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the Apr 6 handoff.

- Logs: we will emit structured JSON as Marissa said. For Splunk ingestion we'll provide a sample HEC token and a CloudWatch->Splunk connector doc if you prefer AWS native exports. No PII fields; prompt_text is never logged.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans, recommended sampling for POC: 10% universal + 100% for error traces. Span attributes include model_variant, request_route, kernel_path, and kv_cache_hit boolean.
- Metrics (priority list):
  * redwood.request.p95_latency_ms
  * redwood.request.p99_latency_ms
  * redwood.request.error_rate
  * redwood.tokens.per_second
  * redwood.cache.hit_rate
  * redwood.model.fallback_rate
  * redwood.estimated_cost_per_1000_tokens

- Dashboard: I've exported a starter Grafana dashboard (sample-grafana-dashboard.json). We can either push to your Grafana tenant or share a read-only preview — Alice, which do you prefer?

I'll prepare the Splunk ingest snippet and sample role + policy and drop them into the Drive folder before Monday.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
